undo/probs: A language model reads four tokens of text. At each step, it gave the right next token a probability of one half, then one quarter, one half, and one eighth.
undo/losses: Each step's loss is minus the log of that probability: zero point six nine, one point three nine, zero point six nine and two point zero eight.
undo/mean: Averaged over the four tokens, the loss is about one point two one per token. True, but hard to picture.
undo/exp: Perplexity undoes the log: it is e to the average loss. e to the one point two one is about three point three six.
count/uniform: Why that is a count: picture a model that spreads its probability evenly over four tokens. It gives the right one a quarter, every time.
count/k: Its loss is the log of four on every token, and e to the log of four is four. Its perplexity is exactly four.
count/means: So a perplexity of three point three six means the model is, on average, as unsure as a fair pick among about three point four tokens.
count/bounds: A model that is always sure and always right scores one, the best possible. One that spreads evenly over a vocabulary of V tokens scores V.
count/compare: Since e to the loss rises with the loss, lower perplexity means lower loss. On the same text and vocabulary, a model at twelve beats a model at thirty.
